key_points.point: The document argues that social media products must protect the mental, physical, and developmental health of American children by ending addictive practices like the endless scroll and targeted advertising to minors. This desire is grounded in the principle that technology companies should not be permitted to design addictive products that harm youth well-being for profit. From a safetyist perspective, safeguarding child development and mental resilience is paramount against the incursions of manipulative digital architectures. The text notes that parents alone cannot make platforms safer and require government-backed safeguards akin to FDA drug safety standards.
key_points.verbatim: Social media products must protect the mental, physical, and developmental health of American children. This includes ending addictive practices like the endless scroll and targeted advertising to minors.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Social media products ought to protect children's mental and developmental health by prohibiting addictive design practices.
key_points.attribution_text: A Desire within safetyist discourse that social media platforms be legally mandated to protect the mental, physical, and developmental health of children by eliminating addictive design elements. Encompasses: youth mental health protection, addictive product design, developmental well-being safeguards.

key_points.point: The document asserts that adversaries like Russia and China are taking advantage of rapidly evolving AI and social media technologies to spread lies, exploit societal divisions, and erode the shared factual basis of democracy. The mechanism involves foreign and domestic actors leveraging platform design to propagate false or misleading information, leaving a third of Americans unable to distinguish truth from falsehood. From a safetyist perspective, this information pollution constitutes a collective loss of societal value and a direct threat to national security. The document highlights that this crisis requires urgent congressional intervention to enforce fact-based information standards.
key_points.verbatim: Social media today is not only robbing children of their social skills and harming their ability to think for themselves, but adversaries like Russia and China are taking advantage of these technologies to spread lies and exploit divisions among Americans.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Foreign adversaries exploit social media and AI technologies to propagate disinformation and erode democratic consensus.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within safetyist discourse that foreign adversaries exploit social media and AI technologies to spread disinformation and erode the shared factual basis of democracy. Encompasses: foreign influence operations, information ecosystem degradation, democratic erosion.

key_points.point: The document calls on Congress to enact responsible safeguards and set government standards for big tech that mirror regulations placed on other addictive products like medicine. The proposed methodology involves establishing statutory principles that mandate privacy, transparency, and child safety protections while restricting data harvesting and manipulative algorithms. From a safetyist perspective, treating big tech under a precautionary regulatory framework prevents corporations from prioritizing profit over public safety. The text acknowledges that Congress has not passed meaningful tech reform since 1996, making a holistic legislative approach urgently necessary.
key_points.verbatim: Today, Issue One and its Council for Responsible Social Media are calling on Congress to holistically address the social media crisis by enacting responsible safeguards and setting the same government standards for big tech that we set for other addictive products.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Enact comprehensive congressional safeguards and government quality standards for big tech analogous to pharmaceutical regulations.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within safetyist discourse that advocates for comprehensive congressional legislation establishing mandatory safety standards and regulatory oversight for social media platforms. Encompasses: statutory regulatory frameworks, addictive product governance, institutional oversight.

key_points.point: The document utilizes public opinion data gathered with Frank Luntz and Citizen Data to establish that roughly 80% of both Republicans and Democrats agree on the necessity of increasing transparency, ensuring privacy, and protecting children from social media harms. This demonstrates a rare cross-partisan consensus that legislators can leverage to overcome decades of gridlock.

The document demands that parents and users have a right to know how social media technology controls content and impacts health through easily understandable system designs. The underlying reasoning is that transparency empowers families to comprehend the mechanics of algorithmic manipulation rather than navigating opaque platform environments. From a skeptic perspective, clear visibility into platform design counteracts corporate information asymmetry and supports public oversight. The text notes that current systems intentionally obscure their operations to maximize user engagement and corporate profit.
key_points.verbatim: We have a right to know how social media technology is controlling the content we see and the impact on our health and wellbeing. Parents should be able to easily understand how these platforms are designed and operated.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Platform transparency ought to be guaranteed so parents and users can easily understand how algorithmic systems operate.
key_points.attribution_text: A Desire within skeptic discourse that transparency mandates be established to ensure users and parents can easily inspect algorithmic system designs and operational impacts. Encompasses: algorithmic transparency, user empowerment, information asymmetry reduction.

key_points.point: The document asserts that big tech platforms routinely collect personal information without express consent and utilize manipulative algorithms solely to maximize corporate profits. The mechanism described is a predatory dataharvesting model where notice-and-choice is subordinated to engagement-driven extraction. From a skeptic perspective, this practice exemplifies coercive data collection that undermines individual privacy and autonomy. The text emphasizes that Congress must intervene to stop platforms from collecting unnecessary consumer data.
key_points.verbatim: No longer can Big Tech be allowed to design addictive products, harvest user data, and manipulate users to maximize their profits with no regard to the consequences.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Big tech platforms extract personal user data without genuine consent to fuel profit-maximizing manipulative algorithms.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within skeptic discourse that major technology platforms extract personal user data without express consent and deploy manipulative algorithms to maximize profits. Encompasses: non-consensual data harvesting, profit-driven algorithmic manipulation, corporate power concentration.

key_points.point: The document advocates for a holistic congressional response that addresses child safety, national security, and data privacy simultaneously rather than treating them in isolation. The proposed approach brings together bipartisan leadership, public opinion research, and civil society advocacy to break through legislative gridlock. From a skeptic perspective, integrating these policy domains prevents corporate lobbyists from exploiting regulatory silos. The text cites polling showing overwhelming bipartisan support across Republicans and Democrats for comprehensive digital reform.
key_points.verbatim: Republicans and Democrats must work together now so that social media no longer poses a threat to our kids and national security.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Synthesize fragmented regulatory efforts into a unified bipartisan legislative agenda addressing child safety, privacy, and national security.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within skeptic discourse that policymakers integrate fragmented regulatory domains to address corporate power and platform harms across child safety, privacy, and national security. Encompasses: cross-domain regulatory coordination, bipartisan legislative strategy, institutional accountability.

factual_claims.claim: More than one in three Americans (34%) have personally experienced or know someone who has been harmed by social media.
Among mothers, nearly half (47%) report knowing someone harmed by social media.
factual_claims.claim_label: Maternal Awareness of Social Media Harm

factual_claims.claim: One-third of all Americans, evenly distributed between Republicans and Democrats, report being unable to distinguish truth from falsehood on social media platforms.
Only 23% of the public responded negatively when asked if the government should address the potential impact of social media.
Eight in 10 Americans hold social media responsible for bullying, childhood mental health struggles, and spreading false information.
Only 7 in 100 Americans view social media's impact on children as more positive than negative.
Eighty-four percent of Republicans and 83 percent of Democrats state that more needs to be done to increase transparency, ensure privacy, and protect children online.

The document does not state that Congress has failed to pass meaningful tech reform since 1996; this claim appears to be an extrapolation or external assertion not directly evidenced in the source text.
